title: Practice Exam 3
description: A third full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam.

questions.question: The maximum speed limit on most California freeways is:
choices: 65 mph unless otherwise posted
55 mph
75 mph
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit on most California freeways is 65 mph. Some freeways are posted at 70 mph, and you must always obey the posted limit.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Maximum Speed Limit

questions.question: When towing a trailer or driving a vehicle with three or more axles, the maximum speed limit is:
choices: 55 mph
65 mph
45 mph
questions.explanation: Vehicles towing trailers, and trucks with three or more axles, are limited to 55 mph on California highways.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Speed Limits for Trucks and Trailers

questions.question: A white rectangular sign on the road is most likely a:
choices: Regulatory sign telling you a law to obey
Warning of a curve
Guide sign showing distances
questions.explanation: White rectangular signs are regulatory signs. They tell you about laws you must obey, such as speed limits or 'No U-Turn.'
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Regulatory Signs

questions.question: A red circle with a red slash over a symbol means:
choices: The action shown is not allowed
The action is recommended
Caution is advised
questions.explanation: A red circle with a diagonal slash indicates a prohibited action, such as 'No Left Turn' or 'No U-Turn.'
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Prohibitory Signs

questions.question: When entering a road from a driveway or alley, you must:
choices: Yield to all traffic and pedestrians on the road
Proceed because you were there first
Sound your horn and pull out
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a private driveway, alley, or parking lot, you must yield to all approaching vehicles and to pedestrians on the sidewalk.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Entering Traffic

questions.question: At a four-way stop, the right of way goes to:
choices: The vehicle that arrived and stopped first
The vehicle on the left
The fastest vehicle
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to come to a complete stop goes first. If two arrive together, the one on the right has the right of way.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Four-Way Stops

questions.question: You should not change lanes while in or near an intersection because:
choices: It is unsafe and other drivers do not expect it
It is always illegal everywhere
It saves no time
questions.explanation: Changing lanes in an intersection is dangerous because turning vehicles and cross traffic do not expect it. Complete lane changes before or after the intersection.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Changing Lanes Safely

questions.question: A center left-turn lane (bordered by solid and broken yellow lines) may be used:
choices: Only to prepare for or complete a left turn
As a regular travel lane
For passing slow traffic
questions.explanation: A two-way center left-turn lane is only for making left turns (or U-turns where legal). It is not a passing or travel lane, and you should not drive in it for more than about 200 feet.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Center Left-Turn Lanes

questions.question: At 55 mph on a dry road, the distance needed to perceive, react, and stop is roughly:
choices: About the length of a football field or more
About one car length
About 20 feet
questions.explanation: At highway speeds, total stopping distance (reaction plus braking) can exceed the length of a football field. This is why following distance and speed control matter so much.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Stopping Distances

questions.question: When a vehicle is tailgating you, the safest response is to:
choices: Increase your following distance from the car ahead and let them pass
Brake suddenly to warn them
Speed up well above the limit
questions.explanation: If someone tailgates you, give yourself more room ahead so you can brake gradually, and move over or slow slightly to let the tailgater pass when safe. Brake-checking is dangerous.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Being Followed Too Closely

questions.question: A first-time DUI conviction in California can result in:
choices: License suspension, fines, and possible jail
A warning only
No consequences for first offenders
questions.explanation: Even a first DUI conviction can mean license suspension, large fines, DUI school, and possible jail time, plus higher insurance costs.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — DUI Penalties

questions.question: By having a California driver license, you have given your consent (implied consent) to:
choices: Chemical testing for alcohol or drugs if lawfully arrested for DUI
Random vehicle searches anytime
Waive all traffic tickets
questions.explanation: Under California's implied consent law, by driving you agree to take a breath or blood test if lawfully arrested for DUI. Refusing leads to automatic license suspension.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Implied Consent Law

questions.question: When you approach a school crossing where a crossing guard is signaling, you must:
choices: Obey the crossing guard's instructions
Follow only the traffic signal
Proceed if no children are visible
questions.explanation: You must obey directions from a school crossing guard, who has authority to stop traffic so children can cross safely.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — School Crossing Guards

questions.question: In a school zone, you should be especially alert because children:
choices: May cross unexpectedly and ignore traffic
Always use crosswalks
Are easy to see at all times
questions.explanation: Children can be unpredictable and may dart into the street without looking. Slow down and scan carefully in school zones.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Driving Near Schools

questions.question: If an ambulance with lights and siren approaches you while you are in an intersection waiting to turn left, you should:
choices: Complete the turn or clear the intersection, then pull over
Stop in the intersection and wait
Reverse out of the intersection
questions.explanation: Never block an intersection. Clear it safely, then pull to the right and stop until the emergency vehicle passes.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Emergency Vehicles

questions.question: On a divided highway, if an emergency vehicle approaches from the opposite side behind a raised median, you:
choices: Generally do not need to stop, but stay alert
Must always stop completely
Must make a U-turn
questions.explanation: On a divided highway with a median, you usually do not need to stop for an emergency vehicle traveling on the opposite side, but remain alert. Always yield when in doubt.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Divided Highways

questions.question: When turning right at a corner, you should watch carefully for:
choices: Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing your path
Only cars behind you
Aircraft overhead
questions.explanation: Right turns are a common place to conflict with pedestrians in the crosswalk and bicyclists going straight. Check carefully before turning.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Turning and Pedestrians

questions.question: Bicyclists in California:
choices: Have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers
Must always ride on the sidewalk
Do not have to obey traffic signals
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and must obey the same rules as drivers. Share the road and treat them as legitimate road users.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Bicyclists' Rights

questions.question: A green painted curb means:
choices: Parking is allowed for a limited time
No parking at any time
Loading zone for freight
questions.explanation: A green curb means parking is allowed for a limited time, shown on a nearby sign or painted on the curb.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Colored Curbs

questions.question: It is illegal to park:
choices: Within 15 feet of a fire hydrant
More than 18 inches from the curb only
On any residential street
questions.explanation: You may not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. Other no-park areas include crosswalks, in front of driveways, and on a sidewalk.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Where You May Not Park

questions.question: If you have a tire blowout on the freeway, you should:
choices: Hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and steer to the shoulder
Brake hard immediately
Speed up to keep control
questions.explanation: In a blowout, grip the wheel firmly, take your foot off the gas, let the car slow gradually, and steer smoothly to the shoulder. Hard braking can cause a skid.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Handling Emergencies

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down on the freeway, you should:
choices: Pull as far right onto the shoulder as possible and turn on hazard lights
Stop in the travel lane and call for help
Stand in the lane to flag down help
questions.explanation: Move as far onto the right shoulder as you can, turn on your hazard lights, and stay aware of traffic. Exit on the side away from traffic if you must leave the vehicle.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Freeway Breakdowns

questions.question: Looking down at a phone to read a text for 5 seconds at 55 mph means you travel about:
choices: The length of a football field without watching the road
Only a few feet
Half a car length
questions.explanation: At 55 mph, five seconds covers roughly 100 yards — the length of a football field — essentially blind. This is why texting while driving is so dangerous.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Dangers of Texting

questions.question: The safest way to handle a phone call you must take while driving is to:
choices: Pull over and stop in a safe place first
Hold the phone low so police can't see
Drive slower and steer with your knees
questions.explanation: Even hands-free calls are distracting. The safest choice is to pull over to a safe spot. Adults may use hands-free if needed, but full attention belongs on driving.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Cell Phones and Driving

questions.question: A steady red traffic light means:
choices: Stop and remain stopped until the light turns green
Slow down and proceed if clear
Stop only if cross traffic is present
questions.explanation: A steady red light means stop. Remain stopped until the light turns green, except for a permitted right turn on red after a complete stop.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: When a traffic signal is not working (completely dark) at an intersection, you should:
choices: Treat it as a four-way stop
Drive through without stopping
Wait until power returns
questions.explanation: When traffic signals are dark due to a power failure, treat the intersection as a four-way stop: stop, then proceed in turn when it is safe.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Inoperative Signals

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic signal means:
choices: You may not turn in that direction until it changes
You may turn after stopping
Yield, then turn
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop and may not make the indicated turn. Wait until a green light or green arrow appears.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Signal Arrows

questions.question: When you intend to turn right, you should position your vehicle:
choices: Close to the right edge of the road or in the right-turn lane
In the center of the road
In the left lane
questions.explanation: Before turning right, move close to the right edge of the road or into the designated right-turn lane, signal, and complete the turn into the nearest right lane.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Making Turns

questions.question: A flashing red light on a railroad crossing signal means:
choices: Stop; a train is approaching
Slow down only
Proceed with caution
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights at a railroad crossing mean stop and wait. Do not cross until the lights stop flashing and any gate has fully raised.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Railroad Crossings

questions.question: When parking uphill without a curb, turn your front wheels:
choices: Toward the edge of the road
Away from the edge of the road
Straight ahead
questions.explanation: Uphill with no curb, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road so a rolling car moves away from traffic. Always set the parking brake.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on Hills

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:
choices: Use high beams on dark open roads but dim them for oncoming traffic
Always use high beams
Drive with parking lights only
questions.explanation: Use high beams on open roads to see farther, but switch to low beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and 300 feet when following another vehicle.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Using Headlights

questions.question: You must turn on your headlights:
choices: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and when visibility is low
Only after midnight
Only on freeways
questions.explanation: Headlights are required from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, and any time you cannot see at least 1,000 feet ahead (rain, fog, etc.). You must also use them when using your wipers.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — When to Use Headlights

questions.question: Marijuana use before driving:
choices: Impairs driving and can lead to a DUI
Is safe if you feel fine
Only affects passengers
questions.explanation: Driving under the influence of marijuana is illegal and dangerous. It slows reaction time and impairs coordination and judgment, and can result in a DUI.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Marijuana and Driving

questions.question: At a crosswalk with a flashing 'Don't Walk' or upraised-hand signal, pedestrians already in the crosswalk:
choices: May finish crossing, and you must let them
Must run back to the curb
Lose the right of way immediately
questions.explanation: Pedestrians who have already started crossing on a 'Walk' signal may finish even after it begins flashing. Drivers must yield until they complete the crossing.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Pedestrian Signals

questions.question: Before you exit the freeway, you should:
choices: Move into the correct exit lane early and slow down on the off-ramp, not the freeway
Brake hard in the travel lane
Cross several lanes quickly at the last moment
questions.explanation: Plan ahead: move to the exit lane in advance, signal, and reduce speed on the deceleration ramp rather than slowing abruptly in the through lanes.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Exiting the Freeway

questions.question: Before making any lane change, the most important thing to do is:
choices: Check that the lane is clear, including your blind spot
Increase your speed
Turn up the radio
questions.explanation: Always make sure the lane you are moving into is clear. Signal, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder to clear your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Safe Lane Changes
